methods.title: Get AI Models
methods.summary: Returns the list of AI segmentation models available in the Aurora pipeline. Call this before RunAISegmentationView so the UI can populate a model picker. Currently returns a hardcoded list containing MedSAM2.

algorithm.text: GET handler with no request parameters. Returns a JSON object with models (string array) and count (integer). On failure returns HTTP 500 with an error message.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[GET / GetAIModelsView] --> B[Build available_models list]
  B --> C[Return models + count]

images.caption: AI model picker populated from the models list

methods.title: Run AI Segmentation
methods.summary: Runs AI-assisted segmentation on a subject scan and merges the result into the existing mask at a chosen label. Loads the full-resolution NIfTI image and mask from the extracted subject folder (or atlas), dispatches to ai_segmentation, then saves both full- and lossy-resolution masks. Use when a user has seeded a rough label region and wants MedSAM2 to refine or expand it.

options.name: directory
options.description: Root data directory containing extracted/ or atlas/ folders.

options.name: subject
options.description: Subject folder name or 'atlas' for atlas data.

options.name: edit
options.description: Edit filename (e.g. scan_lossy.nii.gz). When null, uses the raw subject image as base.

options.name: model
options.description: AI model name to run (currently only 'MedSAM2' is supported).

options.name: current_label
options.description: Label number (1–255) to segment and write into the mask. 0 is reserved for background.

algorithm.text: 1) Validate required POST fields and coerce current_label to int in range 1–255. 2) Resolve base_path (extracted/{subject} or atlas/). 3) Load {full_edit}.nii.gz image and existing or empty {full_edit}.nii.mask.gz mask (via temporary _mask.nii.gz rename for nibabel). 4) Call ai_segmentation(image, mask, current_label, model). 5) Save merged mask at full resolution, then downscale to lossy resolution with scipy.ndimage.zoom (order=0). 6) Return message, segmentation_label, voxels_segmented, and model_used.
algorithm.math: Lossy mask scaling uses per-axis zoom factors z_i = target_shape_i / source_shape_i with nearest-neighbor (order=0) interpolation.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[POST RunAISegmentationView] --> B[Validate params]
  B --> C[Load image + mask NIfTI]
  C --> D[ai_segmentation]
  D --> E[Merge at current_label]
  E --> F[Save full mask]
  F --> G[Scale + save lossy mask]
  G --> H[Return stats]

images.caption: Before/after mask refinement at a selected label using MedSAM2

methods.title: AI Segmentation Dispatcher
methods.summary: Internal dispatcher that routes AI segmentation requests to the correct model implementation. Currently supports MedSAM2 only; raises an exception for unsupported model names. Called by RunAISegmentationView after image and mask volumes are loaded.

options.name: image_data_3d
options.description: 3D medical image volume. Shape (width, height, depth) or (D, H, W); typically uint8 or float32.

options.name: mask_data_3d
options.description: 3D label mask volume, same shape as image. dtype uint8; 0 = background.

options.name: target_label
options.description: Label number to segment (1–255).

options.name: model
options.description: Model name. Supported: 'MedSAM2'.

algorithm.text: If model == 'MedSAM2', delegate to medsam2_segmentation. Otherwise raise Exception with 'Model {model} not supported'. Returns the merged 3D mask array.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[ai_segmentation] --> B{model == MedSAM2?}
  B -->|yes| C[medsam2_segmentation]
  B -->|no| D[Raise unsupported model error]
  C --> E[Return result_mask]

images.caption: Model dispatch flow from API to MedSAM2 backend

methods.title: MedSAM2 Segmentation
methods.summary: Runs MedSAM2 on a 3D volume using the existing mask voxels at target_label to define a bounding box and binary reference mask. Segments within that region, keeps the largest connected component, uses a 3-view ensemble, then merges the result back into the mask at target_label only. Returns the original mask unchanged if no voxels carry the target label.

options.name: image_data_3d
options.description: 3D image volume, shape (D, H, W).

options.name: mask_data_3d
options.description: 3D mask volume, shape (D, H, W), dtype uint8.

options.name: target_label
options.description: Label whose voxels define the bounding box and reference region.

algorithm.text: 1) Find all voxels where mask == target_label; compute axis-aligned bounding box (d_min..d_max, h_min..h_max, w_min..w_max) in (z,y,x) order. 2) Build binary reference_mask (1 at target_label, 0 elsewhere). 3) Instantiate MedSAM2Segmenter(force_cpu=False). 4) Call segmenter.segment with bbox_min/bbox_max, reference mask, use_largest_cc=True, existing_mask_as_reference=True, ensemble=True. 5) Copy mask and set result_mask[segmentation_mask==1] = target_label.
algorithm.math: Bounding box: for label set L = {(d,h,w) | mask[d,h,w]=target_label}, bbox_min=(min d, min h, min w), bbox_max=(max d, max h, max w).
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Find target_label voxels] --> B{Bbox empty?}
  B -->|yes| C[Return mask copy]
  B -->|no| D[Build reference binary mask]
  D --> E[MedSAM2Segmenter.segment]
  E --> F[Merge into result_mask at target_label]
  F --> G[Return result_mask]

images.caption: MedSAM2 bounding box derived from seeded label voxels

methods.title: Edge Detection Slice Preview
methods.summary: Fast 2D slice preview of hysteresis edge detection on a 100³ patch centered at (x,y,z). Uses the same global volume min/max normalization as the full mesh pipeline so slider tuning matches the final result. Caches raw patch and v_min/v_max per scan/edit/position/resolution (max 3 entries).

options.name: directory
options.description: Root data directory.

options.name: filename
options.description: Subject filename or 'atlas'.

options.name: edit
options.description: Edit NIfTI filename; used to resolve volume path.

options.name: full_resolution
options.description: Load full-resolution volume instead of lossy.

options.name: x
options.description: Patch center X coordinate in volume indices.

options.name: y
options.description: Patch center Y coordinate in volume indices.

options.name: z
options.description: Patch center Z coordinate in volume indices.

options.name: low
options.description: Hysteresis low threshold on normalized [0,1] intensities.

options.name: high
options.description: Hysteresis high threshold on normalized [0,1] intensities.

options.name: closing_radius
options.description: Radius (voxels) of the spherical structuring element for binary closing.

algorithm.text: 1) Load or cache 100³ patch and global v_min/v_max. 2) Normalize patch: (patch - v_min)/(v_max - v_min). 3) apply_hysteresis_threshold(low, high). 4) binary_closing with morphology.ball(closing_radius). 5) Return flat uint8 center-Z slices for raw, edges, closed, and filled stages plus patch/volume intensity stats.
algorithm.math: Normalization: \hat{v} = (v - v_{min}) / (v_{max} - v_{min}). Hysteresis keeps pixels above high and connected to high through pixels above low.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[POST slice preview] --> B[Load/cache 100³ patch]
  B --> C[Global min-max normalize]
  C --> D[Hysteresis threshold]
  D --> E[Binary closing ball r]
  E --> F[Return center-Z slices flat]

images.caption: Side-by-side raw, edge, closed, and filled center slices from the preview patch

methods.title: Edge Detection
methods.summary: Full-volume edge detection pipeline: hysteresis thresholding, morphological closing, optional largest-component filtering, then either preview GLB mesh via marching cubes or save the result as a segmentation mask label. When saving permanently from a lossy preview, morphological parameters are scaled up to full resolution. Supports preview-only mesh generation or mask export with force_new_label.

options.name: directory
options.description: Root data directory.

options.name: filename
options.description: Subject filename or 'atlas'.

options.name: edit
options.description: Edit NIfTI filename.

options.name: full_resolution
options.description: Use full-resolution volume for processing.

options.name: preview_only
options.description: When true with save_as_mask false, return GLB mesh preview only.

options.name: force_new_label
options.description: When saving mask and one exists, allocate a new label instead of returning mask_already_exists.

options.name: save_as_mask
options.description: Save binary result as segmentation mask instead of returning mesh.

options.name: low
options.description: Hysteresis low threshold on normalized intensities.

options.name: high
options.description: Hysteresis high threshold on normalized intensities.

options.name: closing_radius
options.description: Binary closing ball radius in voxels.

options.name: largest_component_mode
options.description: Component filter: 'off', 'largest' (keep single largest CC), or 'above_min' (remove objects smaller than min_size).

options.name: min_size
options.description: Minimum connected-component volume in voxels for debris removal.

options.name: fill_mesh
options.description: When true, march cubes on the closed/filled binary mask; when false, march cubes on raw hysteresis edges.

algorithm.text: 1) Load volume and metadata via _load_volume_and_meta. 2) If save_as_mask and not preview_only and not full_resolution, scale closing_radius by resolution_factor and min_size by resolution_factor³. 3) _run_pipeline: normalize, hysteresis, binary closing, optional largest-component or above_min filtering. 4a) Mask path: write .nii.mask.gz with new or merged label; mirror to companion resolution. 4b) Mesh path: swap axes for Babylon, marching_cubes(level=0.5), center and normalize verts, decimate if >250k vertices, return base64 GLB with scale_factor and center.
algorithm.math: Full-res scaling from lossy preview: r' = r \cdot f,\; s' = s \cdot f^3 where f is resolution_factor from lossy_compression metadata.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[POST EdgeDetectionView] --> B[Load volume + spacing]
  B --> C[Scale params if lossy→full save]
  C --> D[Hysteresis + closing + CC filter]
  D --> E{save_as_mask?}
  E -->|yes| F[Write mask label]
  E -->|no| G[Marching cubes → GLB]
  F --> H[Write companion resolution mask]
  G --> I[Return gltf + scale + center]

images.caption: Edge-detection mesh preview generated from hysteresis + morphological closing

methods.title: Deformation-Based MRI Interpolator
methods.summary: Class that converts anisotropic MRI volumes to isotropic voxel spacing using bidirectional ANTs slice registration. Requires exactly one thick axis and two equal thin axes (within 1% tolerance). Used during scan extraction in views.py when anisotropy ratio exceeds 1.1. Default registration_type is SyNOnly for performance.

options.name: registration_type
options.description: ANTs registration method: 'SyNOnly' (elastic only), 'SyN', 'Affine', or 'Rigid'.

options.name: verbose
options.description: Enable progress and diagnostic print output.

algorithm.text: Constructor stores registration_type and verbose. Main entry is interpolate_anisotropic_to_isotropic (see related entry). Internally: auto-detect thick axis as argmax(voxel_size); validate single maximum and equal thin axes; compute target isotropic size as min(thin axes); upsample slice count by scale_factor = thick_size / target_size; for each adjacent slice pair precompute A→B and B→A ANTs SyN deformations; for each target slice position interpolate by scaled deformations and distance-weighted blend of moved A and B slices.
algorithm.math: scale\_factor = s_{thick} / s_{iso},\; N' = \mathrm{round}(N \cdot scale\_factor). Blend weights: w_A = (p - p_A)/(p_B - p_A),\; w_B = 1 - w_A.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[DeformationBasedMRIInterpolator] --> B[interpolate_anisotropic_to_isotropic]
  B --> C[Detect thick axis + validate]
  C --> D[Precompute pair deformations ANTs SyN]
  D --> E[For each target slice position]
  E --> F[Scale + apply A→B / B→A fields]
  F --> G[Blend A_moved and B_moved]
  G --> H[Isotropic volume]

images.caption: Anisotropic thick-slice MRI resampled to isotropic voxels

methods.title: Interpolate Anisotropic to Isotropic
methods.summary: Primary public method on DeformationBasedMRIInterpolator. Converts a 3D anisotropic MRI array to isotropic spacing along the thick axis by registering adjacent 2D slices with ANTs and synthesizing intermediate slices via scaled bidirectional deformation fields and intensity blending.

options.name: image
options.description: Input 3D MRI volume.

options.name: voxel_size
options.description: Voxel dimensions (x, y, z) in mm.

options.name: target_axis
options.description: Axis index (0, 1, or 2) to interpolate. When null, auto-selects the axis with largest voxel size.

algorithm.text: 1) Validate 3D input; pick target_axis = argmax(voxel_size) if None. 2) Require exactly one axis at max size and two equal thin axes (1% tolerance). 3) target_voxel_size = min(thin axes); new slice count = round(N * thick/thin). 4) Build physical position arrays for original and target slices. 5) _bidirectional_deformation_interpolation: normalize slices to [-1,1] for ANTs; for each adjacent pair compute deform_A_to_B and deform_B_to_A via SyNOnly/SyN/Affine/Rigid; for interior target positions scale deformations by weight_A/weight_B, sample source slices with RegularGridInterpolator (linear), blend A_moved*w_B + B_moved*w_A; copy boundary slices unchanged.
algorithm.math: Physical positions: p_i = i \cdot s_{axis}. Per-slice blend: I(p) = w_B \cdot A_{moved} + w_A \cdot B_{moved}.
algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[3D anisotropic image] --> B[Validate axis anisotropy]
  B --> C[Compute new slice grid]
  C --> D[Register adjacent slice pairs ANTs]
  D --> E[Scale deformation fields by distance weight]
  E --> F[RegularGridInterpolator sample + blend]
  F --> G[Isotropic 3D output]

images.caption: Intermediate slices synthesized between thick original slices

methods.title: Interpolate MRI Bidirectional
methods.summary: Module-level convenience wrapper that constructs a DeformationBasedMRIInterpolator and calls interpolate_anisotropic_to_isotropic, casting the result back to the input dtype. Default registration_type is 'SyN' (full SyN) and verbose is true, unlike the class default used in views.py.

options.name: image_array
options.description: 3D numpy array containing MRI data.

options.name: voxel_sizes
options.description: Tuple of (x, y, z) voxel sizes in mm.

options.name: registration_type
options.description: ANTs transform type: 'SyN' (recommended), 'Affine', or 'Rigid'.

options.name: verbose
options.description: Enable progress output during interpolation.

algorithm.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[interpolate_mri_bidirectional] --> B[Create DeformationBasedMRIInterpolator]
  B --> C[interpolate_anisotropic_to_isotropic]
  C --> D[Cast to input dtype]
  D --> E[Return isotropic array]

images.caption: One-call API for bidirectional deformation resampling
